uncited: All methods in this family share the mechanism of decomposing the input volume $V$ into a set of coefficients $C$ using a linear transform, followed by encoding and optional decoding for rendering.
**Transform:** The volume is decomposed using a separable 1D filter bank applied along each axis.
For a 3D volume, this results in subbands representing different frequency components.
In wavelet transforms, these are typically approximation (low-pass) and detail (high-pass) coefficients.
In Laplacian pyramids, they are detail residuals between levels of a Gaussian pyramid [see [Wavelet and Pyramid Transforms](3856-wavelet-and-pyramid-transforms.md)].
The approximation subband from level $j$ is further decomposed at level $j+1$, creating a tree-like structure of coefficients.
This allows for multi-resolution access, where coarse data is available at the root and fine details are deeper in the tree [see [Value compression](6-value-compression.md)].
**Quantization and Entropy Encoding:** Coefficients are quantized (lossy) or kept precise (lossless).
Entropy coding (e.g., Huffman, Arithmetic, Run-Length) is applied to the quantized or raw coefficients to produce the compressed bitstream [see [Value compression](6-value-compression.md)].
**Reconstruction:** To render, the necessary coefficients are decoded and the inverse transform is applied.
This can be done globally (full reconstruction) or locally (block-wise or point-wise) to support adaptive resolution rendering [see [Value compression](6-value-compression.md)].
